requirements.statement: measure how the plugin engine grades large (over 8 MiB), slow-body, and streaming HTTP responses in each of the three execution modes — the Cloudflare isolated runner, the Node isolated runner, and in-process — and record each result against the ADR-0004 probe contract

determine, in each execution mode, whether a probe rejected by a runtime limit (the body-size limit, the subrequest limit, or the CPU-time limit) can be told apart from a network failure or a target error

measure how many monitors one scheduled run can probe on the Cloudflare isolated runner within its per-invocation limits (10 subrequests, 50 ms CPU, 30 s wall time), counting notification deliveries and the per-run configuration re-validation (FR-20) against the same limits, and decide whether a run must be split across invocations
confirm whether the plugin scheduler supports the current 5-minute check cadence
record the spike findings in ADR-0004, and either mark it Accepted or revise it and the affected later phases before engine work (Phase 3) starts
define the public status response (overall and per-site) as one shared, versioned contract that both standalone StatusBeam and the engine plugin produce and the render library consumes

serve the engine plugin's public status, per-site, and badge endpoints with unwrapped response bodies in the same shape as the standalone endpoints, at a documented path mapping from the standalone paths, in the core-owned public status contract (contract version 1, including the optional "not checked yet" flag)

run every configured poll monitor on its schedule from one native plugin in a single scheduled task, on a site that has no sandbox runner configured (webhook-only Sentry monitors take their status from inbound webhooks), and keep check history and the current status snapshot in plugin-owned storage
compute 90-day per-day uptime from plugin storage with the same results as the standalone rollup for the same check history
send Slack and generic-webhook notifications when a monitor's status changes, with every notification secret stored encrypted

accept Statuspage and Sentry inbound webhooks on public endpoints authenticated by a shared secret token, rejecting every request while no webhook secret is configured and comparing the supplied token in constant time
show administrators a status overview of every monitor (current status, 90-day history, latest response time) and a dashboard widget summarizing overall status
classify each check as up, degraded, or down with the same rules and latency measure (time to response headers) a standalone deployment uses
store the monitor configuration as one YAML document validated by the same core schema as a standalone `status.config.yml`

provide an administrator-only plugin admin page where an administrator lists, adds, edits, and removes monitors through a form for each monitor, validated by the core configuration schema and saved only when it is valid
provide a Validate action that checks the configuration without saving it
let an administrator run one monitor's check on demand from the admin page and see its graded status, latency, and response code without recording history or sending a notification
apply plugin-only validation rules on top of the core schema — rejecting configurations the plugin cannot run and warning about ones it can run only partially

keep secrets (the Sentry token, the inbound webhook secret, and the Slack and generic-webhook notification URLs) in encrypted plugin settings that are never returned to the browser, separate from the YAML document
re-validate the stored configuration on every scheduled run before checking anything

provide status banner, 90-day uptime bar, and per-site detail components that a site imports into its own pages, reading the public status contract from a configurable base URL that points at either the engine plugin or a standalone deployment

register the opt-in "statusbeam-status" content block from the same plugin, rendered with the same components, keeping the block's choice of status source (this plugin or a standalone deployment) and the site's allowlist of origins a block may read

document installation and operation of both packages, installing the plugin as a trusted site dependency (a code and configuration change), including the unrestricted outbound network access the engine requests and the probe contract's limits, and state that a plugin-hosted status page goes down with the CMS it reports on
keep the render library and the content block limited to the public status data — no scheduled work, no storage, and no access to engine state
verify contract parity at the HTTP level, comparing the plugin's endpoint responses with the standalone endpoints rather than only the data before it is serialized
convey status in the render library with a label or icon alongside color, using the existing severity tokens (WCAG 2.1 AA)
reuse the core check engine and configuration schema without forking them
restrict the admin page, the dashboard widget, and every admin-only route to site administrators
ship one engine implementation for EmDash, with no sandboxed engine entry, no Block Kit admin page, and no bridge-call sharding
record the native-plugin decision in ADR-0005 and mark ADR-0004 as superseded by it, without rewriting ADR-0004

follow EmDash's admin rules for native React code (its component kit, localization, accessibility, and right-to-left layout), with StatusBeam's own strings available in every locale `@statusbeam/core` supports (en, zh, ja, ko) and English shown for any other admin locale
cover the scheduled run, the public and webhook routes, and the admin routes with tests that execute the plugin the way an EmDash host loads a native plugin
refuse every probe the plugin sends, scheduled or on demand, to a loopback, private, link-local, or cloud-metadata address, as the host's HTTP API does, whichever fetch path the check uses
